name.text: Interpreting the derivative as a limit

questiontext.text:
Which of the following is equal to \(f'({@lim_point@})\) for \(f(x)={@func@}\)

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

[[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

To find the derivative of the function \(f(x) = {@func@}\) at a specific point, \(x = {@lim_point@}\), we can use the limit definition of a derivative (the difference quotient).

The formula for finding the derivative of a function \(f(x)\) at a point \(x = a\) is given by:

\( \displaystyle f'(a) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(a + h) - f(a)}{h}\)

In this case, we want to find \( \displaystyle f'({@lim_point@})\), so \(a = {@lim_point@}\). Therefore, we have:

\( \displaystyle f'({@lim_point@}) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f({@lim_point@} + h) - f({@lim_point@})}{h}\)

Now, plug in the function \(f(x) = {@func@}\):

\( \displaystyle f'({@lim_point@}) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{{@func_coeff@}({@lim_point@} + h)^{@func_power@} - {@func_coeff@}({@lim_point@})^{@func_power@}}{h}\)

Now, simplify the expression inside the limit:

\( \begin{align*} \displaystyle f'({@lim_point@}) &= \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{{@func_coeff@}({@lim_point@} + h)^{@func_power@} -{@num_right@}}{h} \\ &= \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{{@func_coeff@}({@num_left@}) - {@num_right@}}{h} \\ &= \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{{@num_left1@} - {@num_right@}}{h} \\ &= \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{{@func_num@}}{h} \\ &= \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{{@func_num_simp@}}{h} \\ &= \lim_{h \to 0} {@func_num_simp1@} \end{align*} \)

Now, you can evaluate the limit as \(h\) approaches \(0\):

\(\displaystyle f'({@lim_point@}) = {@correct_limit@} \)

So, \( \displaystyle f'({@lim_point@}) = {@correct_limit@}\). This is the derivative of the function \( \displaystyle f(x) = {@func@}\) at \(x = {@lim_point@}\), as found using the limit definition of a derivative.

questionnote.text:
Which of the following is equal to \(f'({@lim_point@})\) for \(f(x)={@func@}\)

\(\lim_{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{{@func_coeff*(lim_point + h)^func_power@} - {@func_coeff*lim_point^func_power@}}{h} \)

Interpreting the derivative as a limit involves understanding how, mathematically, the derivative of a function \( f(x) \) at a point \( x = a \) is defined as \( f'(a) = \lim_{{h \to 0}} \frac{{f(a + h) - f(a)}}{h} \), capturing the instantaneous rate of change as the change in \( x \) (represented by \( h \)) approaches zero.
